messages:
marie: FYI customer acme-corp reported a gap in their SIEM: no audit events between 2026-03-10T13:02:00Z and 2026-03-10T13:07:00Z. S3 lists objects for that window but the SIEM shows nothing. Can we triage?
ingest-bot: alert: forwarder_delivery_failure count spike for tenant=acme-corp window=13:02..13:07 (rule: forwarder-rate-check)
ashish: can you paste the exact S3 keys + a snippet of the forwarder logs? any KMS errors in the logs?
marie: keys: audit/tenant=acme-corp/2026/03/10/13/02/part-0001.gz, part-0002.gz, part-0003.gz (5 objects total for 13:02–13:07). forwarder log excerpt: 
[forwarder] WARN tenant=acme-corp skip batch id=bf3f: checksum mismatch expected=3f2a1b got=7c9d4e
[forwarder] INFO tenant=acme-corp batch-id=bf3f s3key=audit/.../part-0002.gz head-obj-status=200 get-obj-status=206
marie: head-object shows ContentLength: 524288, ContentEncoding: gzip, x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms
but get-object returns fewer bytes and gunzip fails with 'unexpected end of file'
ashish: suspect interplay between multipart uploads, SSE-KMS rewrite, and gzip. Can you run these quick checks and paste outputs?
1) aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit --key "<key>" --query "{CL:ContentLength,CE:ContentEncoding,ETag:ETag, SSE:x-amz-server-side-encryption}"
2) aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-audit --key "<key>" out && ls -l out && gunzip -c out | wc -c
marie: ran head-object, got CL=524288, CE=gzip, SSE=aws:kms. ran get-object -> out size 524000 bytes; gunzip error: "unexpected end of file". So object is truncated compared to ContentLength and gzip integrity fails.
samir: we hit this before: when objects are server-side-rewritten (CopyObject) with SSE-KMS the S3 metadata ContentLength can be wrong if multipart parts were reassembled during rewrite. Some proxies/clients report the original length but the stored payload is slightly different. Forwarder currently validates ContentLength before decrypt/decompress and skips batch if mismatch. That explains the skip.
nashish: what's the forwarder log for the exact skip? any stacktrace?
marie: another log line: 
[forwarder] ERROR tenant=acme-corp batch=bf3f action=forward skip_reason=content-length-mismatch expected=524288 actual=524000
[forwarder] DEBUG forwarder: attempted-decrypt-ok=false error=gunzip: unexpected end of file
security-oncall: what's our exposure surface? Could events be permanently lost? Do we have replays available?
marie: S3 objects exist but appear corrupted/truncated. We need to attempt re-download + decrypt + replay to SIEM. If the stored payload is truncated at the object level, replay might still fail unless S3 has previous versions or we can regenerate from local buffers.
claire-cs: looping in CS: I'll notify the customer about an active investigation and set expectations (no data currently visible, we will attempt a replay/backfill).
ashish: immediate actionable repro steps for eng: 
- reproduce locally using the problematic key: aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-audit --key "<key>" out && sha256sum out && gunzip -t out
- run aws s3api head-object to compare ContentLength and actual bytes
- check S3 object versioning: aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket redwood-audit --prefix "audit/tenant=acme-corp/2026/03/10/13/02/"
samir: mitigation idea: change forwarder to validate content after decryption/decompression rather than trusting head-object ContentLength. For SSE-KMS we must decrypt first then verify size/checksum. Patch: fallback path that, on mismatch, attempts a get-object and validates actual content before skipping. Add a config flag to enable strict mode per-tenant.
marie: temporary support playbook: 1) check for object versions and try get-object on any older version 2) attempt a direct get-object and run gunzip locally to see if any recoverable bytes 3) if versions not available, enqueue tenant for replay/backfill from ingestion buffer (if retention allows) 4) inform CS and customer with ETA
security-oncall: also add incident entry; retention question: do we know how long raw ingestion buffers are kept before compaction? if within 7 days we might backfill.
marie: retention for this tenant: 14 days for raw buffers. We are within window.
nashish: I'll take the forwarder patch (triage + unit test for multipart+SSE case). samir, can you help reproduce and validate with a mocked SSE-KMS rewrite that produced incorrect ContentLength?
samir: yes, I can reproduce with a copy-object that reassembled parts. Will add an integration test.
claire-cs: I'll prepare a customer-facing note: "We identified a forwarding skip due to corrupted gzip payloads after server-side rewrite. Engineering is working on replay and a forwarder fix. We'll follow up with timeline."
marie: action items summarized: 1) CS note (claire) 2) forwarder patch + tests (ashish) 3) reproduction and integration test (samir) 4) attempt replay/backfill for acme-corp 13:00–13:10 (marie) 5) create incident ticket with severity P2 and link logs.
nashish: ack, will open PR with tests.
marie: thanks all. ping me in thread for any blockers. :thumbsup:
